title: Manchester Piccadilly street food traders 'sad to lose home'

evidence_packet.title: Manchester Piccadilly street food traders 'sad to lose home'
evidence_packet.lead: Manchester Piccadilly Market is to close as the redevelopment of Piccadilly Gardens begins
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester Piccadilly Market is to close as the redevelopment of Piccadilly Gardens begins
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Piccadilly street food traders 'sad to lose home' - BBC News Image caption, Leya and Olivia Linsdell said they hope the change will bring new opportunities By Elle McDade North West Published 1 hour ago Street food traders have said they are "sad to lose their home" as Manchester Piccadilly Market prepares to close for the redevelopment of Piccadilly Gardens. The market will shut on 22 October as part of Manchester City Council's multi-million-pound revamp. Traders said they were disappointed to leave a site where they had built a loyal customer base and strong community. The council said all traders would be offered alternative locations. Image caption, Rita's Reign has 25 employees Leya Linsdell, 32, deputy operations manager at family-run Afro-Caribbean food stall Rita's Reign, said she was "incredibly disappointed" after seven years at the site. "We're a family-run business. It's just my mum, dad, sister and me," she said. She said uncertainty over the relocation was worrying, with more than 25 employees relying on the business for their income. 'There will be losses' "It's hard not being able to tell our staff what's going to happen with their jobs, and it's hard for us to make long-term decisions," Linsdell said. Her sister Olivia Linsdell, 30, said: "The change will impact us. There will be losses." While she agreed the area could benefit from the scheme, she said she was concerned the revamp could "take away Manchester's independent businesses". Image caption, A worker at BangGaBangGa, a Korean food vendor fears regular customers will go elsewhere The market is home to traders including Chen's Happy House, BangGaBangGa and Loaded Gyros. Some customers said the closure of the street food stalls would be a "big loss". Regular visitor Steph Bellfield sai

evidence_packet.lead: From the outside, mum Michaela says she looked like "the Instagram mum" but inside she was struggling
evidence_packet.summary: From the outside, mum Michaela says she looked like "the Instagram mum" but inside she was struggling
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A mother says she felt "ashamed" after feeling "completely detached" to her newborn son following his birth four years ago Michaela from Wigan was suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) after four miscarriages and a still birth before her son was born in 2022 "I just felt disbelief, like he wasn't mine. I couldn't make it add up that it could be OK," Michaela said Michaela eventually received help from the Building Attachments and Bonds Support service (BABS), run by Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Trust, which works to connect mothers with their young children Michaela, who is now speaking out to urge others to get help, said she had always wanted to have children "I've always wanted to feel the kicks and get excited," she added

title: Brit Awards boosted Manchester economy by £5m, study finds

evidence_packet.title: Brit Awards boosted Manchester economy by £5m, study finds
evidence_packet.lead: Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig said the awards' move north for the first time was a "massive moment"
evidence_packet.summary: Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig said the awards' move north for the first time was a "massive moment"
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Brit Awards' move to Manchester for the 2026 ceremony generated £5 million for the city and its surrounding area, research has found The annual awards ceremony, widely regarded as the UK's biggest night in music, was hosted in city for the first time this year after being held in the capital for its near 50-year history The move had a positive economic and social impact and created more than 3,000 temporary jobs, according to an independent study conducted by Amion Consulting Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig praised the awards' move north as a "massive moment for our city region", with the 2027 event also set to be held in the city The show took place at Manchester's Co-op Live arena on 28 February in a ceremony hosted by comedian Jack Whitehall, and featuring performances from stars including Harry Styles, Olivia Dean, Raye and Mark Ronson It generated £5m in net additional expenditure in Manchester, with £3.6m coming from visitors and £1.4m as a result of organiser and partner expenditure

title: Ex-world champion boxer Liam Smith charged with apartment building GBH

evidence_packet.title: Ex-world champion boxer Liam Smith charged with apartment building GBH
evidence_packet.lead: The 38-year-old was arrested after an alleged attack on an apartment building's night concierge
evidence_packet.summary: The 38-year-old was arrested after an alleged attack on an apartment building's night concierge
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Ex-world champion boxer Liam Smith charged with apartment building GBH - BBC News Image source, PA Media Image caption, Liam Smith had been due to make a comeback fight against local fighter Ilari Kujala in Finland on 4 September By Jonny Humphries North West Published 30 September 2026 Former world champion boxer Liam Smith has been charged with causing grievous bodily harm after an alleged attack on a night concierge at a luxury Manchester apartment building. Smith, who held the WBO light-middleweight title from 2015 to 2016, was arrested after the man suffered serious facial injuries at The Blade on Silvercroft Street in Deansgate on 13 September, police confirmed. The 38-year-old appeared at Manchester Magistrates Court the following day charged with causing GBH with intent, and was released on bail. Smith, from Liverpool, is next due to appear at Manchester Crown Court on 19 October, where he will be asked to enter a plea. Image source, PA Media Image caption, Smith earned a memorable victory against Chris Eubank Jr in 2023 The alleged victim reportedly suffered fractures and required surgery. Smith, nicknamed Beefy, had been due to make a comeback fight against local fighter Ilari Kujala in Finland on 4 September. However, he withdrew from the fight a few days earlier after suffering a calf injury, according to reports. Smith has fought at the highest levels, including against elite champions such as Saul 'Canelo' Alvarez. More recently he fought British rival Chris Eubank Jr in two memorable bouts, defeating the Brighton man in the first fight in January 2023 before suffering a defeat in the rematch eight months later. title: Rochdale Council wins 'Downton Shabby' High Court case

evidence_packet.title: Rochdale Council wins 'Downton Shabby' High Court case
evidence_packet.lead: Hopwood DePree took the council to court in his bid to take over the Grade II-listed mansion for £1
evidence_packet.summary: Hopwood DePree took the council to court in his bid to take over the Grade II-listed mansion for £1
evidence_packet.evidence_text: An American man has lost his legal bid to take ownership of a historic mansion for £1 Hopwood DePree, who claims ancestral links to the Grade II-listed Hopwood Hall in Middleton, Rochdale, said he was "incredibly disappointed" after a judge at the High Court in Manchester ruled against him DePree, an actor and filmmaker, argued a 2017 agreement with Rochdale Council gave him the option to buy the manor house after securing planning permission to restore and redevelop it However, Judge David Hodge KC found the conditions required for ownership of the property to transfer had not been met Despite its current state, Hopwood Hall was described as being in the top 10% of most important listed buildings in England, the court heard DePree's plans included a wedding venue, hotel accommodation and visitor attractions aimed at bringing the hall back to life

title: Oasis unheard recordings pulled from auction after band 'sue'

evidence_packet.title: Oasis unheard recordings pulled from auction after band 'sue'
evidence_packet.lead: The auction house said it was "very disappointed" the lot could no longer be sold
evidence_packet.summary: The auction house said it was "very disappointed" the lot could no longer be sold
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oasis unheard recordings pulled from auction after band 'sue' - BBC News Image source, Reuters Image caption, The 63 tapes feature sound checks and live performances recorded by sound engineer Huw Richards Published 30 September 2026 A set of unheard Oasis recordings valued at between £1.2m and £1.6m have been pulled from an auction after the band filed an injunction. Earlier this month, it was announced that Littleton Auctions, in Evesham, were selling a set of recordings which included 63 live shows , as well as soundchecks and more than 100 hours of Noel and Liam Gallagher in the 1990s. They were collected by Oasis sound engineer Huw Richards, who worked with the band from the release of their debut album Definitely, Maybe in 1994, until 2001. However, the auction house said the sale of the recordings had been suspended after the band intervened. Managing director Ben Homer said: "Littleton Auctions confirms that the Oasis recordings known as The Desk Tapes have been withdrawn from our October 3 auction in light of legal proceedings. "We are very disappointed that we cannot offer this significant archive as planned." More stories in Hereford & Worcester 'Why we flushed away Dragons' Den investment' Published 6 days ago Police hope for new leads in 2001 attack as woman reveals how life changed Published 2 days ago Reform takes legal advice over 'crazy' council letter Published 2 days ago The recordings were brought to sale by the sound engineer's son Owain Richards, who said: "It is true that Oasis have sued me and my father to try to prevent the auction of the tapes made by my father many years ago. "We have agreed to postpone the auction [of the tapes] to enable the legal dispute to be resolved either by litigation or otherwise in an orderly way." Image source, Marc

title: Manchester Airport reviews parking following traffic complaints

evidence_packet.title: Manchester Airport reviews parking following traffic complaints
evidence_packet.lead: Taxi drivers complain about standing traffic on roads around Terminal 2, leading to delayed pick-ups
evidence_packet.summary: Taxi drivers complain about standing traffic on roads around Terminal 2, leading to delayed pick-ups
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Airport reviews parking following traffic complaints - BBC News Image source, DC Travel Image caption, Several taxi firms have reported long queues on roads around Manchester Airport's Terminal 2 in recent months By Richard Stead North West Published 30 September 2026 Parking arrangements at Manchester Airport are being reviewed after several taxi firms reported significant road traffic congestion in recent months. They have complained about standing traffic on routes around Terminal 2, leading to significant delays in picking up passengers. Abu Bakar, from MCR Elite Transfers, said: "It's very frustrating for me because I am wasting time in traffic and it takes its toll on you because it makes you tired." Manchester Airport said it was carrying out an "extensive review" and referred to "a range of factors including lower passenger-to-vehicle ratios caused by greater numbers of couples and solo travellers arriving in cars compared to the summer months". Image caption, Abu Bakar from MCR Elite Transfers said there has been significant traffic congestion outside Terminal 2 at Manchester Airport in recent months Bakar added: "All of the time I am stuck in traffic means I'm losing money and my earnings are going to drop because of the congestion at the airport. "It's been a problem for months and some of my passengers have had to wait for up to 30 minutes." Other taxi firms have complained on social media about long queues on roads near Terminal 2. A spokesperson for the airport added: "We are carrying out an extensive review of the system to identify ways of mitigating these issues. "In the short term we have deployed extra traffic marshals to help keep things moving and we are working with Transport for Greater Manchester to change the timing of traffic lights

title: John Stones misses speeding letter while at World Cup with England

evidence_packet.title: John Stones misses speeding letter while at World Cup with England
evidence_packet.lead: The England defender drove his £150,000 Range Rover at 43mph near his Cheshire home, a court hears
evidence_packet.summary: The England defender drove his £150,000 Range Rover at 43mph near his Cheshire home, a court hears
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Footballer John Stones has been convicted of speeding after he missed a police letter while at the World Cup with England The 32-year-old defender, who left Manchester City for Inter Milan in the summer, was caught driving his £150,000 Range Rover at 43mph (69 km/h) along a 30 mph (48 km/h) stretch of a country lane near his Cheshire home in May Stones admitted being the driver when first contacted by Cheshire Police, but did not respond to a second letter offering him the chance to pay a fixed penalty to keep the speeding offence out of court He wrote to Warrington Magistrates Court to explain he had been abroad but was landed with a £1,052 court bill. He was given four points Stones was prosecuted after he did not reply to the police letter The Three Lions star was convicted in the Single Justice Procedure, with a magistrate last week issuing him four penalty points and ordering him to pay a £666 fine, £120 in costs, and a £266 victim surcharge

title: Salford Royal surgery unit fails to improve rating

evidence_packet.title: Salford Royal surgery unit fails to improve rating
evidence_packet.lead: Inspectors said patients were treated with kindness and compassion, but a range of concerns remained
evidence_packet.summary: Inspectors said patients were treated with kindness and compassion, but a range of concerns remained
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Surgery services at a Greater Manchester hospital have been rated as requiring improvement after an inspection found further work was needed to ensure patients received safe and timely care The Care Quality Commission (CQC) found Salford Royal Hospital had made enough progress to comply with a warning notice issued in October 2025 over staffing levels and risk management, but identified 12 breaches of regulations relating to patient safety, governance and staffing The inspection was carried out in May following concerns about staffing, governance and safety processes in gynaecology, spinal surgery and neurosurgery Karen Coverley, deputy chief nursing officer, said the trust was pleased inspectors had recognised improvements Inspectors said some staff had not completed life-support training relevant to their roles, infection-control standards remained below trust targets and incidents were not always investigated in a timely manner The report also highlighted concerns over waiting times, discharge delays and patient readmission rates following surgery

evidence_packet.lead: The Brit Awards' move to Manchester for the 2026 ceremony generated £5 million for the city and its surrounding area, research has found The annual awards ceremony, widely regarded as the UK's biggest night in music, was hosted in city for the first time this year after being hel
evidence_packet.summary: The Brit Awards' move to Manchester for the 2026 ceremony generated £5 million for the city and its surrounding area, research has found The annual awards ceremony, widely regarded as the UK's biggest night in music, was hosted in city for the first time this year after being hel
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Brit Awards' move to Manchester for the 2026 ceremony generated £5 million for the city and its surrounding area, research has found The annual awards ceremony, widely regarded as the UK's biggest night in music, was hosted in city for the first time this year after being held in the capital for its near 50-year history The move had a positive economic and social impact and created more than 3,000 temporary jobs, according to an independent study conducted by Amion Consulting Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig praised the awards' move north as a "massive moment for our city region", with the 2027 event also set to be held in the city The show took place at Manchester's Co-op Live arena on 28 February in a ceremony hosted by comedian Jack Whitehall, and featuring performances from stars including Harry Styles, Olivia Dean, Raye and Mark Ronson It generated £5m in net additional expenditure in Manchester, with £3.6m coming from visitors and £1.4m as a result of organiser and partner expenditure

evidence_packet.summary: An American man has lost his legal bid to take ownership of a historic mansion for £1 Hopwood DePree, who claims ancestral links to the Grade II-listed Hopwood Hall in Middleton, Rochdale, said he was "incredibly disappointed" after a judge at the High Court in Manchester ruled a
evidence_packet.evidence_text: An American man has lost his legal bid to take ownership of a historic mansion for £1 Hopwood DePree, who claims ancestral links to the Grade II-listed Hopwood Hall in Middleton, Rochdale, said he was "incredibly disappointed" after a judge at the High Court in Manchester ruled against him DePree, an actor and filmmaker, argued a 2017 agreement with Rochdale Council gave him the option to buy the manor house after securing planning permission to restore and redevelop it However, Judge David Hodge KC found the conditions required for ownership of the property to transfer had not been met Despite its current state, Hopwood Hall was described as being in the top 10% of most important listed buildings in England, the court heard DePree's plans included a wedding venue, hotel accommodation and visitor attractions aimed at bringing the hall back to life

evidence_packet.summary: A set of unheard Oasis recordings valued at between £1.2m and £1.6m have been pulled from an auction after the band filed an injunction Earlier this month, it was announced that Littleton Auctions, in Evesham, were selling a set of recordings which included 63 live shows , as wel
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A set of unheard Oasis recordings valued at between £1.2m and £1.6m have been pulled from an auction after the band filed an injunction Earlier this month, it was announced that Littleton Auctions, in Evesham, were selling a set of recordings which included 63 live shows , as well as soundchecks and more than 100 hours of Noel and Liam Gallagher in the 1990s They were collected by Oasis sound engineer Huw Richards, who worked with the band from the release of their debut album Definitely, Maybe in 1994, until 2001 However, the auction house said the sale of the recordings had been suspended after the band intervened Managing director Ben Homer said: "Littleton Auctions confirms that the Oasis recordings known as The Desk Tapes have been withdrawn from our October 3 auction in light of legal proceedings "We are very disappointed that we cannot offer this significant archive as planned."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Parking arrangements at Manchester Airport are being reviewed after several taxi firms reported significant road traffic congestion in recent months They have complained about standing traffic on routes around Terminal 2, leading to significant delays in picking up passengers Abu Bakar, from MCR Elite Transfers, said: "It's very frustrating for me because I am wasting time in traffic and it takes its toll on you because it makes you tired." evidence_packet.evidence_text: Footballer John Stones has been convicted of speeding after he missed a police letter while at the World Cup with England The 32-year-old defender, who left Manchester City for Inter Milan in the summer, was caught driving his £150,000 Range Rover at 43mph (69 km/h) along a 30 mph (48 km/h) stretch of a country lane near his Cheshire home in May Stones admitted being the driver when first contacted by Cheshire Police, but did not respond to a second letter offering him the chance to pay a fixed penalty to keep the speeding offence out of court He wrote to Warrington Magistrates Court to explain he had been abroad but was landed with a £1,052 court bill. He was given four points Stones was prosecuted after he did not reply to the police letter The Three Lions star was convicted in the Single Justice Procedure, with a magistrate last week issuing him four penalty points and ordering him to pay a £666 fine, £120 in costs, and a £266 victim surcharge

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Urmston Fly-tipping fury in Urmston as residents slam latest pile of dumped furniture Councillor Jo Harding highlighted her concern after furniture had been dumped on the roadside News Elizabeth Cotton TV and Celebrity Writer 19:29, 30 Sep 2026 View 2 Urmston residents have expressed their outrage as they hit out after more waste dumped in fly-tipping scandal on the roadside. Council bosses in Manchester are increasing fines for fly-tipping to the ‘absolute legal limit’ in a ‘landmark’ move to crackdown on illegal dumping as i Offenders who are caught will soon face being slapped with a £1,000 penalty rather than the previous lower amount of £700. In the last 12 months nearly 18,000 fly-tipping incidents were recorded in the city, leading to the removal of more than 5,000 tonnes of waste However, it hasn't acted as a deterrent for people yet, as Councillor Jo Harding took to Facebook to condemn those responsible for leaving the waste behind over the weekend in Urmston She wrote: “If you dumped this at the top of Railway Road over the weekend, shame on you. The teams will move asap but honestly, this is disgraceful behaviour. There isn’t a fly-tipping fairy.” Accompanying pictures showed a full sofa and armchair set along with cushions, a bar stool and a mattress had been left on the pavement just before the Crofts Bank Road junction

Labour councillors representing Stretford and Humphrey Park in Trafford raised concerns after the lights at the ‘quite busy’ Robin Hood crossroads in Stretford ke The junction – at Urmston Lane, Kingsway and Barton Road – was upgraded as part of a £17.6m redevelopment of Stretford town centre. The project outside Stretford Mall on Kingsway was finished in 2024 with new green spaces, planting, footpaths and a cycle lane But nearby traffic lights kept going out, with three incidents reported on September 3 2025, December 16 2025 and June 30 2026 Coun Steve Adshead, Trafford council’s executive member for Highways and Environmental Services and Stretford councillor, said: “For them to go several times less than a couple of years old seemed very odd.” While the lights were fixed, it didn’t solve the problem. evidence_packet.lead: Middleton Hopwood Hall High Court hearing judgement as council victorious over US actor Hopwood DePree The two-day trial ruled in favour of the council following long saga over the future of Hopwood Hall Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Re An American filmmaker has be
evidence_packet.summary: Middleton Hopwood Hall High Court hearing judgement as council victorious over US actor Hopwood DePree The two-day trial ruled in favour of the council following long saga over the future of Hopwood Hall Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Re An American filmmaker has be
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Middleton Hopwood Hall High Court hearing judgement as council victorious over US actor Hopwood DePree The two-day trial ruled in favour of the council following long saga over the future of Hopwood Hall Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Re An American filmmaker has been denied in his bid to buy Middleton ’s Hopwood Hall for the nominal sum of £1 following a ‘sad day’ at the High Court. Hopwood DePree’s dream to restore the historic building has been left in tatters. The US-born Middletonian claims ancestral roots t A wedding and hospitality venue, a hotel ‘retreat’, gift shop and guided tours of the facility were all touted in Mr DePree’s original vision He signed an exclusivity agreement with Rochdale council – also known as an options agreement – back in 2017. But the town hall ended that agreement in October 2024 Mr DePree believed the local authority acted unlawfully by denying his ‘legally binding’ option to buy Hopwood Hall. The council felt there was a lack of progress in enacting the agreement, despite granting planning permission for the Grade-II* listed building’s change of use in The war has rumbled on over the two years afer the agreement was torn up. The matter was taken to the High Court at Manchester Civil Justice Centre this week

However, bosses have yet to produce an offer the union can put to its members, according to Unison The union adds that those negotiating on behalf of NCA are seeking to clarify what the trust is willing to offer UNISON North West regional organiser Kevin Dolan said: "There was hope the trust was serious about ending the dispute, but that doesn’t appear to be the case at this moment

title: Parking firm responds after dad hit with £170 fine following M&S visit after breaking strict rule

evidence_packet.title: Parking firm responds after dad hit with £170 fine following M&S visit after breaking strict rule
evidence_packet.lead: Stockport Parking firm responds after dad hit with £170 fine following M&S visit after breaking strict rule 'We understand that receiving a parking charge can be frustrating' Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 17:04, 30 Sep 2026 Upda A parking firm has responded
evidence_packet.summary: Stockport Parking firm responds after dad hit with £170 fine following M&S visit after breaking strict rule 'We understand that receiving a parking charge can be frustrating' Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 17:04, 30 Sep 2026 Upda A parking firm has responded
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Parking firm responds after dad hit with £170 fine following M&S visit after breaking strict rule 'We understand that receiving a parking charge can be frustrating' Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 17:04, 30 Sep 2026 Upda A parking firm has responded following criticism from a dad who was given a £100 parking fine - later hiked to £170 - after he nipped to Marks & Spencer. Tim Coates parked up to shop at the M&S at the Peel Centre in Stockport on June 22 this year and ‘didn’t think anything of it’ The firm says cars must be completely between the white lines of the parking bay. A photo seen by the Manchester Evening News taken when the fine was issued shows Mr Coates’ tyre on the white line Mr Coates was slapped with a £100 fine, which the dad later appealed . He said: “Due to the car parked next to me, I couldn’t park any closer or I couldn’t get the pram out “There’s literally one tyre on the white line. They said I was obstructing someone from parking in the bay next to me. I tried to appeal it, [asking for] a common sense policy if you have got a child in the car. I needed the space.” The appeal was later rejected but Mr Coates said he never received notification of this until a debt collector’s letter came through. He claims this meant he missed the window of opportunity to either pay the fine before it increased to £170 or appeal it further

The si According to planning documents submitted as part of the plan, the existing property on the site will be kept alongside a green corridor to the south of the site Part of the site will be kept as green space with ‘high quality’ trees ‘retained and preserved where possible’ and new public space created The homes will be a mix of housing types including 78 flats and ‘will result in a well planned residential development of which will echo the vernacular of the surrounding area, and will therefore be easily absorbed into its immediate context’ The documents say the plans will maintain ‘the character and quality of the area’ while helping address housing needs

Payam Postchi is due to appear at Manchester Magistrates' Court later today (September 30) Greater Manchester Police says the 36-year-old, of Greenway Close, Bury , is a British national of Iranian origin. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Urmston Fly-tipping fury in Urmston as residents slam latest pile of dumped furniture Councillor Jo Harding highlighted her concern after furniture had been dumped on the roadside News Elizabeth Cotton TV and Celebrity Writer 19:29, 30 Sep 2026 View 2 Urmston residents have expressed their outrage as they hit out after more waste dumped in fly-tipping scandal on the roadside. Council bosses in Manchester are increasing fines for fly-tipping to the ‘absolute legal limit’ in a ‘landmark’ move to crackdown on illegal dumping as i Offenders who are caught will soon face being slapped with a £1,000 penalty rather than the previous lower amount of £700. In the last 12 months nearly 18,000 fly-tipping incidents were recorded in the city, leading to the removal of more than 5,000 tonnes of waste However, it hasn't acted as a deterrent for people yet, as Councillor Jo Harding took to Facebook to condemn those responsible for leaving the waste behind over the weekend in Urmston She wrote: “If you dumped this at the top of Railway Road over the weekend, shame on you. The teams will move asap but honestly, this is disgraceful behaviour. There isn’t a fly-tipping fairy.” Accompanying pictures showed a full sofa and armchair set along with cushions, a bar stool and a mattress had been left on the pavement just before the Crofts Bank Road junction

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stretford Slugs break traffic lights at busy crossroads in Stretford The bizarre explanation has been offered by transport bosses Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 18:42, 30 Sep 2026 View 3 Images The traffic lights at the junction The mysterious reason new traffic lights in Stretford kept failing – causing traffic chaos – has now been discovered. Labour councillors representing Stretford and Humphrey Park in Trafford raised concerns after the lights at the ‘quite busy’ Robin Hood crossroads in Stretford ke The junction – at Urmston Lane, Kingsway and Barton Road – was upgraded as part of a £17.6m redevelopment of Stretford town centre. The project outside Stretford Mall on Kingsway was finished in 2024 with new green spaces, planting, footpaths and a cycle lane But nearby traffic lights kept going out, with three incidents reported on September 3 2025, December 16 2025 and June 30 2026 Coun Steve Adshead, Trafford council’s executive member for Highways and Environmental Services and Stretford councillor, said: “For them to go several times less than a couple of years old seemed very odd.” While the lights were fixed, it didn’t solve the problem. evidence_packet.lead: Middleton Hopwood Hall High Court hearing judgement as council victorious over US actor Hopwood DePree The two-day trial ruled in favour of the council following long saga over the future of Hopwood Hall Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Re An American filmmaker has be
evidence_packet.summary: Middleton Hopwood Hall High Court hearing judgement as council victorious over US actor Hopwood DePree The two-day trial ruled in favour of the council following long saga over the future of Hopwood Hall Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Re An American filmmaker has be
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Middleton Hopwood Hall High Court hearing judgement as council victorious over US actor Hopwood DePree The two-day trial ruled in favour of the council following long saga over the future of Hopwood Hall Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Re An American filmmaker has been denied in his bid to buy Middleton ’s Hopwood Hall for the nominal sum of £1 following a ‘sad day’ at the High Court. Hopwood DePree’s dream to restore the historic building has been left in tatters. The US-born Middletonian claims ancestral roots t A wedding and hospitality venue, a hotel ‘retreat’, gift shop and guided tours of the facility were all touted in Mr DePree’s original vision He signed an exclusivity agreement with Rochdale council – also known as an options agreement – back in 2017. But the town hall ended that agreement in October 2024 Mr DePree believed the local authority acted unlawfully by denying his ‘legally binding’ option to buy Hopwood Hall. The council felt there was a lack of progress in enacting the agreement, despite granting planning permission for the Grade-II* listed building’s change of use in The war has rumbled on over the two years afer the agreement was torn up. The matter was taken to the High Court at Manchester Civil Justice Centre this week

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre Convicted murderer who now says he's innocent in stand-off with Manchester council as he refuses to leave hotel room 'They want me to leave... it's not happening' Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 18:18 A convicted murderer who has gone back on his guilty plea says he is trapped in a hotel room - again - amid a stand-off with Manchester council. Stephen Kidd was locked up in 2009 for his part in the killing of a man the previous year The 54-year-old was released from prison in January 2025 having served 17 years. Mr Kidd suffered a stroke behind bars and now uses a wheelchair He soon found himself living in a windowless room at the Britannia Hotel on Portland Street in Manchester city centre . Mr Kidd said he was unable to secure social housing accommodation and was spending £1,600 a month from his benefits on the room He told the Manchester Evening News last year he was a changed man and that he wanted to get a job and contribute to society. evidence_packet.title: Parking firm responds after dad hit with £170 fine following M&S visit after breaking strict rule
evidence_packet.lead: Stockport Parking firm responds after dad hit with £170 fine following M&S visit after breaking strict rule 'We understand that receiving a parking charge can be frustrating' Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 17:04, 30 Sep 2026 Upda A parking firm has responded
evidence_packet.summary: Stockport Parking firm responds after dad hit with £170 fine following M&S visit after breaking strict rule 'We understand that receiving a parking charge can be frustrating' Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 17:04, 30 Sep 2026 Upda A parking firm has responded
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Parking firm responds after dad hit with £170 fine following M&S visit after breaking strict rule 'We understand that receiving a parking charge can be frustrating' Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 17:04, 30 Sep 2026 Upda A parking firm has responded following criticism from a dad who was given a £100 parking fine - later hiked to £170 - after he nipped to Marks & Spencer. Tim Coates parked up to shop at the M&S at the Peel Centre in Stockport on June 22 this year and ‘didn’t think anything of it’ The firm says cars must be completely between the white lines of the parking bay. A photo seen by the Manchester Evening News taken when the fine was issued shows Mr Coates’ tyre on the white line Mr Coates was slapped with a £100 fine, which the dad later appealed . He said: “Due to the car parked next to me, I couldn’t park any closer or I couldn’t get the pram out “There’s literally one tyre on the white line. They said I was obstructing someone from parking in the bay next to me. I tried to appeal it, [asking for] a common sense policy if you have got a child in the car. I needed the space.” The appeal was later rejected but Mr Coates said he never received notification of this until a debt collector’s letter came through. He claims this meant he missed the window of opportunity to either pay the fine before it increased to £170 or appeal it further

Bury council and developer Bruntwood have said they want to ‘better connect’ the shopping centre with the world-famous Bury Ma Full details of what the money will be spent on are yet to come. However, the pot is expected to help the council deliver on priorities set out in the Mill Gate Regeneration Framework, developed in 2024 Those priorities included a ‘large area of demolition’ within the shopping centre itself, along with the removal of part of the roof around Union Street and the TJ Hughes store. Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Every morning at 11 almost exactly on the dot, a group of men gather on the ground floor of the Northern Quarter Car Park: that tall, graffiti-coated building on the corner of Church and Tib Street One by one they unlock the padlocks dangling from the back of their flat-tyred vans, and the doors swing open. Out from within comes cart after cart full of corn This is the not-entirely-secret HQ of the Market Street corn vendors: a four-storey council-owned car park, sitting across two of Manchester’s busiest streets. When I get there, the men are working in silence, hands sheathed in black gloves, bags of sweetcorn torn open, cardboard Just as I’m about to approach a vendor, I’m forwarded an email from a reader. It has the subject line The Mystery We All Want Solved "The reason I’m writing is because the people of Manchester are desperate to know what the hell is going on with all of the corn sellers on Market St "Why are there now so many of them? How on earth do they make a profit? Are they independent vendors or all part of the same company? Is their presence legal? What does their proliferation say about the state of the city centre?”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Hopwood DePree, who claims ancestral links to the Grade II-listed Hopwood Hall in Middleton, Rochdale, said he was "incredibly disappointed" after a judge at the High Court in Manchester ruled against him DePree, an actor and filmmaker, argued a 2017 agreement with Rochdale Council gave him the option to buy the manor house after securing planning permission to restore and redevelop it However, Judge David Hodge KC found the conditions required for ownership of the property to transfer had not been met Despite its current state, Hopwood Hall was described as being in the top 10% of most important listed buildings in England, the court heard DePree's plans included a wedding venue, hotel accommodation and visitor attractions aimed at bringing the hall back to life However, Rochdale Council decided in 2022 not to transfer ownership of the hall to DePree and later locked him and a group of volunteers out of the site

title: Motion tabled to celebrate centenary of women's voting equality

evidence_packet.title: Motion tabled to celebrate centenary of women's voting equality
evidence_packet.lead: In 2028 it will be 100 years since women were granted the right to vote on equal terms with men
evidence_packet.summary: In 2028 it will be 100 years since women were granted the right to vote on equal terms with men
evidence_packet.evidence_text: In 2028 it will be 100 years since women were granted the right to vote on equal terms with men Although some women were granted the right to vote in 1918, it was not until 1928 that all women over the age of 21 were granted the vote regardless of their occupation, wealth or ownership of property To mark this hugely significant milestone a Council motion has been set out to recognise and celebrate this moment in history It is no secret that Manchester played a huge part in the Women’s Suffrage movement. The Pankhurst name is known across the globe and is a byword for resilience and a refusal to give in to apparent insurmountable odds In 2018 a statue of Emmeline Pankhurst was proudly installed in St Peter’s Square and has since become a rallying point for people across the city to have their voices heard, and acts as a powerful reminder that history was made by women who refused to give up But the Pankhursts were also joined by thousands of ordinary Mancunian women whose names have been lost to history, but whose legacy still lives on a century later

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Cllr Thomas Robinson has been chosen as the new Deputy Leader of Manchester City Council He fills the role vacated by Cllr Garry Bridges when he was elected Leader earlier this month and will serve alongside the other Deputy Leader, Cllr Tracey Rawlins His portfolio responsibilities will include work and skills, crime and safety and emergency planning Cllr Robinson has served as Executive Member for Health and Social Care since 2022 overseeing the adult social care service which was recently rated ‘Good’ by the Care Quality Commission, and has represented Clayton and Openshaw as a councillor since 2021 Raised in Ardwick, he has deep roots in Manchester and his experience growing up in a council flat amid a supportive community has shaped his commitment to public service and building a city where everyone can thrive regardless of background “As a born and bred Mancunian, to become the Deputy Leader of our city is truly humbling. A formal direction was served under Section 77 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994, requiring those at the encampment to leave and remove their The Council also provided information about authorised sites in Greater Manchester, along with advice about health, wellbeing and reporting hate crime After the direction was not followed, the Council began court proceedings. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. evidence_packet.summary: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live […] The post Beat the Jams Autumn season announced appeared first on Band on the Wall
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

evidence_packet.evidence_text: It’s been a busy week at Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, with technology, growth and devolution featuring heavily in many of the conversations we’ve been part of In his first Conference speech as Prime Minister, Andy Burnham talked about devolving more power to places, backing businesses to grow and taking some of what has worked in Greater Manchester into a wider national approach. He also confirmed that AI will be a central focus of the That felt particularly relevant following an event we hosted through the UK Tech Cluster Group with AI Minister Kanishka Narayan, North East Mayor Kim McGuinness and other regional leaders, looking at AI, devolution and local growth One of the clearest themes from the discussion was that devolution should not mean every place trying to build the same thing. Different regions have different strengths, assets and specialisms, and there was a strong view that greater collaboration between places could create bi Procurement and buying local also featured strongly. The discussion highlighted the role public sector buying power can play in supporting regional businesses, helping successful pilots move into commercial contracts and strengthening UK capability in areas such as AI and cyber There was also a broader conversation about sovereignty and the UK’s role internationally. The discussion was not about trying to own every part of the AI stack, but about understanding where the UK already has genuine capability and where it makes sense to build more. Strengths

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised. More capital is being concentrated in fewer companies while the market for exits remains difficult Financial news recently added another dimension to that discussion. AI-related shares fell last week after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower approach to the development of increasingly capable AI models. Nvidia finished the day down 3.4%, SoftBank fell 10.7% in Tokyo Additionally, the Bank of England is predicted to increase interest rates later this year, which could affect the North West's tech funding landscape by raising the cost of capital across the board, compressing valuations, pushing investors toward profitability over growth-at-all The British Business Bank's 2026 Small Business Equity Tracker found that equity investment into UK smaller businesses fell 4% to £12.3bn in 2025. Seed deal numbers fell 27% and venture deals fell 13%. AI companies attracted 44% of all investment into smaller businesses while the Beauhurst recorded £14.4bn of UK equity investment across 2,799 deals in the first half of 2026 but three AI companies accounted for 29% of all the capital raised. Those very large rounds can make the overall market look stronger than it feels to businesses raising at seed or Ser Beauhurst's analysis shows that UK equity investment more than doubled between 2017 and 2021 to £32.2bn while annual exits remained at around 400 to 500. An exit takes a median of four years from a funding round

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A unique classical concert which aims to improve the experience of people with hearing loss who want to enjoy music is coming to Manchester this October Academics from the Cadenza Project, working with the Manchester Camerata orchestra, are inviting people with and without hearing loss to a special research show at the Stoller Hall on Thu 29 Oct. The concert will feature Beethoven’s Symphony No. 6, the Pastoral Symphony The Cadenza project, led by the University of Salford, is researching how to improve music for people with hearing loss. The free concert is a unique opportunity to shape future research on hearing aids while enjoying live music Trevor Cox, Professor of acoustic engineering at the University of Salford, explains: “We don’t think anything like this has been attempted before. When people suffer hearing loss, the main treatment is a hearing aid. But the devices are designed for speech. Music is an afterthou “But music is such an important part of our lives, it brings us together for shared experiences that people with hearing issues can feel locked out of. Live classical music is particularly hard for hearing aids to deal with, as it ranges from extremely quiet to very louder, over “This is a unique opportunity for people, both with hearing problems and those who hear normally, to help shape future research on hearing aids while enjoying the fabulous Camerata.”

It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and t
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester United FC Man United latest: INEOS hatch masterplan for Michael Carrick as £74m star issued fresh message Michael Carrick will want to get Manchester United's season back on track when club football returns Comments Sport Jake Bayliss 05:30, 01 Oct 2026 Manchester United may not return to competitive action until later this month, but Michael Carrick will have plenty to occupy him during the international break. The United manager is seeking answers following his team's underwhelming start to the campaign Carrick will be closely monitoring those on international duty, with Noussair Mazraoui among the latest to cause concern for his boss. Речной круиз органично сочетается с атмосферой яркого клубного действа, а увлекательное путешествие открывает город с нового, почти кинематографичного ракурс Autumn Boat Party собирает не только путешественников, стремящихся увидеть британскую столицу в новом свете, но и тех, для кого Лондон давно стал родным домом. Это возможность хотя бы на один вечер оставить городскую суету на берегу и погрузиться в атмосферу свободы, живой музыки Когда солнце медленно скрывается за горизонтом, а огни набережных отражаются в темных водах Темзы, город обретает свою глубину и очарование. Именно в такие мгновения Autumn Boat Party превращается в вечер, наполненный теплым общением, осенней романтикой и неповторимой атмосферой Чтобы попасть на вечеринку AUTUMN BOAT PARTY в Лондоне, покупайте билеты на нашем сайте и в кассах города.
